Subject: Skyline Health - billing-tag passthrough + redaction requirement - priority for Q2 close

Team — quick context: Skyline Health (prospect -> PO pending) is asking for two linked capabilities as gating items for signature: (1) the ability to propagate an arbitrary per-request billing tag (they call it a chargeback tag) through our inference stack so tokens can be attributed back to their internal metering system, and (2) an enforceable, contract-backed redaction of PHI from any logs/exports by default with customer-configurable retention windows (they want 90 days redaction by default, with an option to request an audited exception).

Why this matters: this is a potential $1.2M ARR account with procurement timeline that wants signoff by Apr 20. Legal and procurement have signaled they will not execute without explicit technical controls and an attestation we can meet their billing attribution needs.

Ask: can Product + Eng prioritize a short scoped deliverable we can present as EAP to Skyline? Minimal must-haves I heard from them: header-level passthrough of a tag (they suggested X-RI-Billing-Tag), visible in audit exports; server-side redaction hook that removes PHI before any long-term logs are written and a retention toggle. I've attached the Skyline POC spec and a draft SOW they sent.

If we can't do full token-level per-token attribution quickly, what is a reasonable phased approach that keeps the deal alive? Happy to take a 30m sync — I'm booking time but wanted to surface now.

Thanks,
Mina Haddad
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
mina.haddad@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0193

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Skyline Health - billing-tag passthrough + redaction requirement - priority for Q2 close

Thanks Mina — high level reaction from Eng: both asks are doable but have different complexity and risk profiles.

1) Billing-tag passthrough: We can accept a simple request header (e.g., X-RI-Billing-Tag) at the ingress gateway and thread it through to our telemetry and audit export pipeline. That will allow Skyline to join token counts and per-request metadata on their side. This is the lowest-friction path and should not require model runtime changes.

2) Token-level cost attribution: If they want exact per-token cost attributed to the tag inside the runtime (i.e., token-by-token joinable assertion in our billing records), that requires instrumenting the runtime to persist the tag with each KV-cache item and make small changes to our accounting pipeline — moderate risk and potential latency noise.

3) Redaction: We can implement a pre-log redaction hook that runs before data is written to long-term storage. Options: regex-based scrubbing (fast but brittle), or a light PII classifier + deterministic scrub pipeline (better precision, slightly more CPU). We also need to think about auditability: Skyline will likely request proofs that redaction happened (hashes, redaction logs), and they may ask for a way to run periodic verification — that expands scope.

Questions for Product/Customer:
- Do they require raw unredacted logs retained anywhere for compliance/audit?
- Are they comfortable with header-level passthrough initially while we work on runtime attribution?
- Do they require KMS/CMEK for the exported metadata or a customer-managed key for audit artifacts?

Rough estimate for a minimal EAP: header passthrough + basic regex redaction hook + audit flag: 2 eng sprints + 1 QA sprint. Adding full token attribution and attestation/reporting: additional 2 sprints and requires a small billing infra change. If we prioritize immediately, we can aim for an EAP in ~6 weeks.

I'll prep a short tech note mapping changes to services.

— Ben

Subject: Re: Skyline Health - billing-tag passthrough + redaction requirement - priority for Q2 close

Good summary. Product view / next steps:

Acceptance criteria (proposed minimal EAP):
- Ingress accepts X-RI-Billing-Tag and surfaces it on per-request telemetry and in audit export CSV.
- A configurable pre-log redaction hook runs (configurable list + default PHI regex set) and ensures any redacted items are replaced with deterministic tokens.
- Admin toggle for retention window (default 90d) and exportable redaction attestations (simple timestamped record that redaction ran).

Scope exclusions for EAP: full per-token billing join, long-term attestation reports or external KMS integration — these can be follow-ons.

We need to assess product impact: will other customers be affected if we add header passthrough? Ben, pls include a risk note if this could allow tag spoofing or leak tags across tenants.

I propose a 30-minute sync Friday to align scope and confirm timeline. Mina — please invite the Skyline contacts and legal if possible.

Laura Bennett
Product Manager, Platform
laura.bennett@redwood.com

Adding customer context from CS/Legal:
- Procurement will not sign without a technical attestation that PHI is not stored in cleartext for longer than the retention window. They asked for a short redaction proof we can include as an appendix to the SOW.
- They also require SAML SSO + SCIM provisioning as part of the onboarding.
- Timeline: legal wants the attestation + SOW final by Apr 20; procurement may push earlier. If we cannot provide an EAP with those controls, they will delay signature and look at alternatives.

Mina, can you confirm if Skyline's execs are flexible on a phased delivery (header passthrough first) or if they insist on token-level attribution up front? I'm prepared to escalate if needed.

— Monica

Folks — attaching a short PoC plan (see Skyline-POC-specs.pdf). Technical proposal summary:
- Phase 1 (PoC/EAP, ~6 weeks if prioritized): accept X-RI-Billing-Tag at gateway, surface tag in telemetry & audit export; implement pre-log redaction using a lightweight PII model + deterministic replacement. Provide a simple redaction-attestation artifact (JSON with request id, redaction timestamp, redaction rules applied).
- Phase 2 (follow-on, +2 sprints): instrument runtime to persist tag per-request in accounting events for exact per-token joins, and add optional KMS integration for audit artifacts.

Estimated effort: Eng (Ben +2) ~ 3 sprints for Phase 1 including QA and infra changes; Phase 2 additional 2 sprints. If we pull in a small task force (Eng/Product/QA) and make this a priority, we can get EAP in 6 weeks.

Temporary workaround (to keep deal moving): we can offer a signed attestation that we will use header-level tags and provide a daily redacted audit export accessible to Skyline for reconciliation. This avoids runtime touches and buys time to implement token attribution.

Attachments: Skyline-POC-specs.pdf, Skyline-Procurement-Questionnaire.xlsx, Skyline-SOW-draft.docx

Thanks — we appreciate the rapid responses. A few clarifications from Skyline Legal/Infra:
- Header-level passthrough is acceptable as Phase 1 provided we receive a redacted daily audit export and a signed attestation that PHI is not present in cleartext in long-term storage.
- We still need the option for a 90-day retention window default and the ability to request an exception for audited reviews.
- Data residency: all logs and audit artifacts must remain in the US.

If you can confirm these points and provide an ETA for the PoC artifacts, our procurement/legal teams can proceed with the SOW sign-off contingent on the EAP timeline.

Looking forward to the sync.

— Emma Torres
